findings.evidence: On an all-healthy endpoint the posterior concentrates on the least-failure-prone hypothesis (observed: healthy probe set drove MAP >= 0.25 without any fault). The 19-hypothesis space has no explicit "no fault / healthy" hypothesis, so healthy evidence has no place to go and settles on the hypothesis whose signature failure probabilities are smallest.
findings.root_cause: likelihood table encodes failure modes only; healthy outcomes lack a dedicated hypothesis
findings.impact: a healthy network can display a >=25% "diagnosis" for a failure mode; mitigated in N1.1 by the established no-claim rule (no failure evidence -> no hypothesis, refusal preserved), so no false conclusion is reachable, but the displayed MAP on healthy endpoints is an artifact
findings.fix: deferred: consider an explicit Healthy/None hypothesis in a later phase (N5 math refinement) with audit-approved likelihood rows
findings.verification: observed live in the N1.1 oracle/refusal tests; refusal path proven honest (n1_insufficient_evidence_refusal_preserved)

findings.evidence: Live observation on this machine (censorship environment): HTTP to 127.0.0.1:1 (nothing listening, raw connect times out at the TCP layer) returns HTTP 503 to the reqwest client — loopback HTTP is transparently intercepted by the environment's network stack. Result: the tcp layer measures the direct path (Failed) while the tls/http layers measure an intercepted path (Ok + 503) — contradictory layer evidence for one probe, and "unreachable endpoint" probes can report Ok at the HTTP layer.
findings.root_cause: reqwest client inherits the environment interception; no explicit direct-path enforcement
findings.impact: layer semantics corrupted under interfered-with networks (exactly where NANI matters most); the Bayesian engine handles the contradiction honestly but the evidence quality is degraded; health classification of unreachable endpoints can be wrong
findings.fix: deferred decision (N1.3 or dedicated ticket): consider reqwest .no_proxy() + explicit direct-path handling for health probes, OR an explicit "intercepted" outcome category — requires design review; do not change silently
findings.verification: reproduced live during N1.1 test development (direct probe to port 1 answered 503); recorded in N1_01/N1_05

findings.evidence: predict() names its parameter delta_seconds and calibrates mix = exp(-0.001 * delta) for seconds, while CORRELATION_WINDOW_MS = 300000 compares against raw timestamp deltas (ms semantics). The two conventions contradict; with ms timestamps a 1s gap would mix ~63% of the posterior away.
findings.root_cause: unit ambiguity between the transition kernel (seconds) and the correlation window constant (ms)
findings.impact: no production caller existed before N1.1; N1.1 resolves it at the call site by passing unix SECONDS (correct predict semantics; the correlation window then spans a bounded investigation, which is the intended within-investigation discount). Engine-internal harmonization still pending.
findings.fix: deferred: harmonize units inside diagnosis.rs (N5 hygiene) — call-site resolution documented in N1_01
findings.verification: unit analysis in reports/N1_01_BAYESIAN_ENGINE_INTEGRATION_MAP.md
findings.resolution_evidence: N1.2 (d46ece9): the ms->seconds conversion now lives at ONE canonical boundary (observe_diagnostic_probes[_matching], monitor.rs); both production feeders route through it - the investigation path committed, the manual health-check path (concurrent author WIP, commands/nani.rs) converted in its working tree, commit pending with that author. Regression tests: k1_* suite incl. the comparative tripwire (converted ~0.42 vs buggy ~0.24 over ten confirming probes). STILL OPEN: the engine-internal unit ambiguity (delta_seconds calibration vs CORRELATION_WINDOW_MS in ms) - engine untouched by design; a newtype (Seconds/Timestamp wrapper) is the durable fix, deferred to N5 hygiene.
